htn_kidney.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) refers to structural or functional abnormalities of the kidneys caused by various factors lasting ≥3 months, or a decline in glomerular filtration rate (GFR) of <60 mL/min of unknown cause lasting ≥3 months. Its primary causes include diabetic kidney disease, hypertensive nephropathy, IgA nephropathy, membranous nephropathy, and lupus nephritis, among others. As a new class of antidiabetic drugs, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) have been shown in numerous clinical studies and animal experiments to be effective in treating CKD of various etiologies. The renoprotective effects of SGLT2 inhibitors are independent of their glucose-lowering effects....

portal_hypertension.abstract: Focal nodular hyperplasia (FNH) is widely recognized as one of the leading benign hepatic neoplasms encountered in clinical practice, disproportionately affecting women during their third through fifth decades of life. Although generally asymptomatic, FNH may occasionally present with acute abdominal pain, as illustrated in our case of a young woman with symptomatic giant FNH. Ultrasound, computed tomography, and MRI constitute the main imaging modalities used in the diagnostic evaluation of FNH, each contributing complementary information; however, distinguishing it from malignant hepatic tumors may remain challenging, particularly in atypical presentations. portal_hypertension.abstract: Cystic Fibrosis-associated Hepatobiliary involvement (CFHBI) refers to a wide range of liver and biliary-related clinical and/or biochemical abnormalities that impact people with cystic fibrosis. Advanced cystic fibrosis liver disease (aCFLD) describes individuals with advanced fibrosis or cirrhosis and/or portal hypertension. The current review discusses both CFHBI and aCFLD in terms of pathogenesis; clinical, imaging and biochemical manifestations; screening, monitoring, and management recommendations; and the impact of cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) modulator therapy.

portal_hypertension.abstract: Since its introduction in 1992, the Rex shunt (also called Meso-Rex bypass, MRB) has substantially advanced the management of pediatric extrahepatic portal vein obstruction (EHPVO) by restoring physiological hepatopetal portal flow. However, a comprehensive synthesis of the accumulating evidence and evolving practices is notably lacking, especially given that the latest Baveno VI consensus was published nine years ago in 2016. This review aims to synthesize three decades of advances in Rex shunt evolution, from a novel technique to a widely adopted first-line surgical option.
